stem: The four sides of a spinner are $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$. The spinner is supposed to be fair, but Sonam suspects that the spinner is biased so that the probability, $p$, that it will land on side $A$ is greater than $\frac{1}{4}$. He spins the spinner 10 times and finds that it lands on side $A$ 6 times.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Test Sonam’s suspicion using a 1% significance level.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: Later Sonam carries out a similar test at the 1% significance level, using another 10 spins of the spinner.
parts.text: Calculate the probability of a Type I error.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Assuming that the value of $p$ is actually $\frac{3}{5}$, calculate the probability of a Type II error.
